listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, October 14, 2026. The lead story: Pope Leo XIV had surgery on Tuesday to remove a cancerous growth in his lung, the Vatican announced. The pope is the head of the Catholic Church. The summary does not give details about his recovery. Other front page stories. Dre Greenlaw, a linebacker for the San Francisco 49ers, will sit out Monday night's game against the Commanders after the NFL denied his appeal. Ukraine's president says Russian strikes left 600,000 people without power, and at least three were killed. A federal judge ruled that the president cannot bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House coverage until a formal trial. Georgia voters began early voting, citing cost of living, taxes and political leadership. Now the sections. Tech and AI: Anthropic describes building its own source control system after a sharp rise in code changes. Politics: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign as US ambassador to Greece over allegations she sought payment from a Trump donor for access. World: Saudi-led coalition forces struck a fuel depot near Sanaa, and missiles were intercepted near Riyadh. Sports: Andre Fili won a first-round knockout, and Brendan Allen won by submission in round five. Atlanta: Senators Jon Ossoff and Mike Collins clashed in a heated debate ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Architecture: Matterport now imports registered point cloud files, useful for scan-to-model workflows. Science and Nature: Mars appears beside the Beehive cluster under an aurora over Sweden, and scientists describe 57 new species in an Argentine deep-sea canyon. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican says
lead.note: Pope Leo XIV had surgery on Tuesday to remove a cancerous growth in his lung, the Vatican announced. The announcement came from the Vatican itself, which confirmed the diagnosis and the surgery. The pope is the head of the Catholic Church, so the news reaches well beyond Rome and the Vatican. The summary does not include details about his recovery or next steps, so those remain unknown from this report. It is the most significant story in today's brief for many readers, and it arrived as a short, direct announcement. Additional coverage may follow as more details are released.
